text: For vehicles with a lower bumper height of less than 425 mm, the lower legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 4.1.1 shall be applied.
condition: lower bumper height less than 425 mm

text: For vehicles with a lower bumper height greater than or equal to 425 mm and less than 500 mm, the requirements of either paragraph 4.1.1 or 4.1.2, at the choice of the manufacturer, shall be applied.
condition: lower bumper height greater than or equal to 425 mm and less than 500 mm

text: For vehicles with a lower bumper height greater than or equal to 500 mm, the upper legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 4.1.2 shall be applied.
condition: lower bumper height greater than or equal to 500 mm

text: To verify compliance with the performance requirements of paragraph 5.1.1, both the flexible lower legform impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.1.1 and the test procedures specified in paragraph 7.1.1 shall be used.
condition: lower legform to bumper test applies

text: To verify compliance with the performance requirements of paragraph 5.1.2, both the upper legform impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.1.2 and the test procedures specified in paragraph 7.1.2 shall be used.
condition: upper legform to bumper test applies

text: To verify compliance with the child headform performance requirements of paragraph 5.2.1, both the child headform impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.2.1 and the test procedures specified in paragraphs 7.2 and 7.3 shall be used.

To verify compliance with the adult headform performance requirements of paragraph 5.2.2, both the adult headform impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.2.2 and the test procedures specified in paragraphs 7.2 and 7.4 shall be used.
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1 (flexible lower legform to bumper), the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22 mm.
condition: when tested with the flexible lower legform impactor

text: When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1, the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.
condition: when tested with the flexible lower legform impactor

text: When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1, the maximum dynamic posterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.
condition: when tested with the flexible lower legform impactor

text: When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1, the absolute value of dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm.
condition: when tested with the flexible lower legform impactor, outside nominated relaxation widths

text: The manufacturer may nominate bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total where the absolute value of the tibia bending moment shall not exceed 380 Nm.
condition: in bumper test widths nominated by the manufacturer as relaxation zone, unless restricted by the Contracting Party

text: A Contracting Party may restrict application of the tibia bending moment relaxation zone requirement in its domestic legislation if it decides that such restriction is appropriate.
condition: Contracting Party option

text: When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.2 (upper legform to bumper), the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.
condition: when tested with the upper legform impactor

text: When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.2 (upper legform to bumper), the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.
condition: when tested with the upper legform impactor

text: When tested as a DPPS, the headform test conditions and requirements in Annex 1 shall apply.
condition: vehicle equipped with a DPPS tested as a DPPS

text: For child headform tests to the front structure in accordance with paragraphs 7.2, 7.3 and, if applicable, Annex 1, the HIC shall comply with paragraph 5.2.3.
For adult headform tests to the front structure in accordance with paragraphs 7.2, 7.4 and, if applicable, Annex 1, the HIC shall comply with paragraph 5.2.3.
The HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over a minimum of one half of the child headform test area.
condition: vehicle has both child and adult headform test areas

text: The HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the combined child and adult headform test areas.
condition: vehicle has both child and adult headform test areas

text: The HIC for the remaining areas of the headform test areas shall not exceed 1,700 for both headforms.
condition: vehicle has both child and adult headform test areas

text: In case there is only a child headform test area, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the test area.
condition: only a child headform test area exists

text: In case there is only a child headform test area, the HIC shall not exceed 1,700 for the remaining area.
condition: only a child headform test area exists

text: The manufacturer shall identify the zones of the bonnet top where the HIC must not exceed 1,000 (HIC1000 Zone) or 1,700 (HIC1700 Zone).

Marking of the bonnet top impact area and of the HIC1000 Zone and HIC1700 Zone shall be based on a drawing supplied by the manufacturer, viewed from a horizontal plane above the vehicle parallel to the vehicle horizontal zero plane.

The manufacturer shall supply a sufficient number of x and y co-ordinates to mark up the bonnet top, HIC1000 Zone and HIC1700 Zone areas on the actual vehicle while considering the vehicle outer contour in the z direction.

The HIC1000 Zone and HIC1700 Zone may consist of several parts, the number of parts not being limited; the impacted zone shall be determined by the first contact point of the headform with the bonnet top.

The calculation of the surface of the impact area and of the HIC1000 Zone and HIC1700 Zone surface areas shall be done on the basis of a projected bonnet viewed from a horizontal plane parallel to the horizontal zero plane above the vehicle, using the drawing data supplied by the manufacturer.
At the time of testing, the test facility and the vehicle or sub-system shall have a relative humidity of 40 percent ± 30 percent.
At the time of testing, the test facility and the vehicle or sub-system shall have a stabilized temperature of 20 + 4 ºC.
The impact test site shall consist of a flat, smooth and hard surface with a slope not exceeding 1 percent.
Either a complete vehicle or a cut-body, adjusted to the conditions of paragraphs 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.1.2, shall be used for the test.
The vehicle shall be in its normal ride attitude and shall be either securely mounted on raised supports or at rest on a flat horizontal surface with the parking brake applied.
condition: complete vehicle used for test

text: The cut-body shall include all parts of the vehicle front structure, all under-bonnet components and all components behind the windscreen that may be involved in a frontal impact with a vulnerable road user.
condition: cut-body used for test

text: The cut-body shall be securely mounted in the normal vehicle ride attitude.
condition: cut-body used for test

text: All devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test.
condition: vehicle fitted with devices to protect vulnerable road users

text: The manufacturer shall be responsible for showing that any devices designed to protect vulnerable road users will act as intended in a pedestrian impact.
condition: vehicle fitted with devices to protect vulnerable road users

text: Vehicle components which could change shape or position, other than active devices to protect pedestrians, and which have more than one fixed shape or position shall require the vehicle to comply with the components in each fixed shape or position.
condition: component has more than one fixed shape or position
applies_to: system or component that changes position

text: When tested as a DPPS, the vehicle shall be adjusted as specified in the test procedure defined in Annex 1.
condition: vehicle tested as a DPPS

text: The flexible lower legform impactor shall consist of the flesh and skin, flexible long bone segments (representing femur bone and tibia bone), and the knee joint as shown in Figure 12.
The assembled flexible lower legform impactor shall have a total mass of 13.2 ± 0.4 kg.

The dimensions of the fully assembled flexible lower legform impactor shall be as defined in Figure 12, measured at the vertical centre line; brackets, pulleys, protectors, connection parts, etc. attached for launching and/or protection may extend beyond the dimensions and tolerances shown in Figures 12 and 13.
The cross-sectional shape of the femur main body segments, the tibia main body segments and their impact faces of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be as defined in Figure 13 (a).
The cross-sectional shape of the knee joint of the flexible lower legform impactor and its impact face shall be as defined in Figure 13 (b).
The mass of the femur of the flexible lower legform impactor without the flesh and skin, including the connection parts to the knee joint, shall be 2.46 ± 0.12 kg.
The mass of the tibia of the flexible lower legform impactor without the flesh and skin, including the connection parts to the knee joint, shall be 2.64 ± 0.13 kg.

The mass of the knee joint of the flexible lower legform impactor without the flesh and skin shall be 4.28 ± 0.21 kg, the screws that attach femur and tibia to the knee being part of the knee assembly.
The assembled mass of the femur, the knee joint and the tibia of the flexible lower legform impactor without the flesh and skin shall be 9.38 ± 0.3 kg.
The centres of gravity of the femur and tibia of the flexible lower legform impactor without the flesh and skin, including the connection parts to the knee joint, shall be as defined in Figure 12.
The centre of gravity of the knee joint of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be as defined in Figure 12.

The moment of inertia of the femur of the flexible lower legform impactor without the flesh and skin, including the connection parts inserted to the knee joint, about the X-axis through its centre of gravity shall be 0.0339 ± 0.0016 kgm².

The moment of inertia of the tibia of the flexible lower legform impactor without the flesh and skin, including the connection parts inserted to the knee joint, about the X-axis through its centre of gravity shall be 0.0486 ± 0.0023 kgm².
The moment of inertia of the knee joint of the flexible lower legform impactor about the X-axis through its centre of gravity shall be 0.0180 ± 0.0009 kgm².

For each test, the flexible lower legform impactor (femur, knee joint and tibia without flesh and skin) shall be covered by the flesh and skin composed of synthetic rubber sheets (R1, R2) and foamed neoprene sheets (N1F, N2F, N1T, N2T, N3) as shown in Figure 14.
The size of the flesh and skin sheets of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be within the requirements described in Figure 14.
The flesh and skin sheets of the flexible lower legform impactor shall have compression characteristics as shown in Figure 15.
The compression characteristics of the flexible lower legform impactor flesh and skin sheets shall be checked using material from the same batch as the sheets used for the impactor flesh and skin.

All flexible lower legform impactor components shall be stored for a sufficient period of time in a controlled storage area with a stabilized temperature of 20 ± 4°C prior to impactor removal for testing.
After removal from the storage, the flexible lower legform impactor shall not be subjected to conditions other than those in the test area as defined in paragraph 6.1.1.
Four transducers shall be installed in the tibia of the flexible lower legform impactor to measure bending moments at locations within the tibia, at the sensing locations defined in Figure 16.
Three transducers shall be installed in the femur of the flexible lower legform impactor to measure bending moments applied to the femur, at the sensing locations defined in Figure 16.
Three transducers shall be installed in the knee joint of the flexible lower legform impactor to measure elongations of the MCL, ACL and PCL, at the measurement locations shown in Figure 16.
The knee ligament elongation measurement locations of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be within ± 4 mm along the X-axis from the knee joint centre.
The instrumentation response value CFC, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 180 for all transducers of the flexible lower legform impactor.
The CAC response value, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 30 mm for the knee ligament elongations of the flexible lower legform impactor.
The CAC response value, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 400 Nm for the tibia and femur bending moments of the flexible lower legform impactor.
The determination of all flexible lower legform impactor peak tibia bending moments and ligament elongations shall be limited to the assessment interval (AI).
The flexible lower legform impactor shall meet the performance requirements specified in paragraph 8.
The flexible lower legform impactor shall be certified according to the inverse certification (IC) test procedure of paragraph 8.1.3 before starting a vehicle test series.
After a maximum of 10 vehicle tests, the flexible lower legform impactor should be certified according to the pendulum certification (PC) test procedure of paragraph 8.1.2.
Ongoing certification testing of the flexible lower legform impactor shall constitute the sequence IC – PC – PC – IC – PC – PC – etc. with a maximum of 10 tests between each certification.
The flexible lower legform impactor shall be certified according to the procedures of paragraph 8.1 at least once a year.
The upper legform impactor shall be rigid, foam covered at the impact side, and 350 ± 5 mm long.
The total mass of the upper legform impactor including those propulsion and guidance components which are effectively part of the impactor during the impact shall be 9.5 kg ± 0.1 kg.

The total mass of the upper legform impactor front member and other components in front of the load transducer assemblies, together with those parts of the load transducer assemblies in front of the active elements, but excluding the foam and skin, shall be 1.95 ± 0.05 kg.
The upper legform impactor for the bumper test shall be mounted to the propulsion system by a torque limiting joint and be insensitive to off-axis loading.

The upper legform impactor shall move only in the specified direction of impact when in contact with the vehicle and shall be prevented from motion in other directions including rotation about any axis.
The torque limiting joint of the upper legform impactor shall be set so that the longitudinal axis of the front member is vertical at the time of impact with a tolerance of ± 2°.
The joint friction torque of the upper legform impactor torque limiting joint shall be set to a minimum of 650 Nm but no more than 850 Nm.

The centre of gravity of those parts of the upper legform impactor which are effectively forward of the torque limiting joint, including any weights fitted, shall lie on the longitudinal centre line of the impactor, with a tolerance of ± 10 mm.
The length between the load transducer centre lines of the upper legform impactor shall be 310 ± 1 mm.
The front member diameter of the upper legform impactor shall be 50 ± 1 mm.
For each test the upper legform impactor foam flesh shall be two new sheets of 25 mm thick foam type CF45 or equivalent, cut from the sheet of material used for the dynamic certification test.
The skin of the upper legform impactor shall be a 1.5 mm thick fibre reinforced rubber sheet.

The mass of the upper legform impactor foam and rubber skin together shall be 0.6 + 0.1 kg, excluding any reinforcement, mountings, etc. used to attach the rear edges of the rubber skin to the rear member.

The upper legform impactor foam and rubber skin shall be folded back towards the rear, with the rubber skin attached via spacers to the rear member so that the sides of the rubber skin are held parallel.

The upper legform impactor foam shall be of such a size and shape that an adequate gap is maintained between the foam and components behind the front member, to avoid significant load paths between the foam and these components.

The upper legform test impactor or at least the foam flesh shall be stored during a period of at least four hours in a controlled storage area with a stabilized humidity of 35 percent ± 15 percent and a stabilized temperature of 20 ± 4 °C prior to impactor removal for test.
After removal from the storage the upper legform impactor shall not be subjected to conditions other than those pertaining in the test area.
The upper legform impactor front member shall be strain gauged to measure bending moments in three positions, each using a separate channel, with the strain gauges on the back of the front member.
The two outer strain gauges of the upper legform impactor shall be located 50 ± 1 mm from the impactor's symmetrical axis and the middle strain gauge on the symmetrical axis with a ± 1 mm tolerance.

Two load transducers shall be fitted to the upper legform impactor to measure individually the forces applied at either end of the impactor, plus strain gauges measuring bending moments at the centre and at positions 50 mm either side of the centre line.
The instrumentation response value CFC, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 180 for all transducers of the upper legform impactor.
The CAC response value, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 10 kN for the force transducers of the upper legform impactor.
The CAC response value, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 1,000 Nm for the bending moment measurements of the upper legform impactor.
The upper legform impactor shall meet the performance requirements specified in paragraph 8.
The certified upper legform impactor may be used for a maximum of 20 impacts before re-certification (this limit does not apply to propulsion or guidance components).
The upper legform impactor shall be re-certified if more than one year has elapsed since the previous certification.
condition: if more than one year has elapsed since the previous certification

text: The upper legform impactor shall be re-certified if any impactor transducer output, in any impact, has exceeded the specified CAC.
condition: if any transducer output has exceeded the specified CAC

text: The child headform impactor shall be made of aluminium, be of homogenous construction and be of spherical shape.
The overall diameter of the child headform impactor shall be 165 ± 1 mm.
The mass of the child headform impactor shall be 3.5 ± 0.07 kg.
The moment of inertia of the child headform impactor about an axis through the centre of gravity and perpendicular to the direction of impact shall be within the range of 0.008 to 0.012 kgm2.
The centre of gravity of the child headform impactor including instrumentation shall be located in the geometric centre of the sphere with a tolerance of ± 2 mm.
The child headform impactor sphere shall be covered with a 14 ± 0.5 mm thick synthetic skin, which shall cover at least half of the sphere.

A recess in the child headform impactor sphere shall allow for mounting one triaxial or three uniaxial accelerometers within ± 10 mm seismic mass location tolerance from the centre of the sphere for the measurement axis, and ± 1 mm for the perpendicular direction to the measurement axis.

In the child headform impactor, one of the uniaxial accelerometers shall have its sensitive axis perpendicular to the mounting face A and its seismic mass positioned within a cylindrical tolerance field of 1 mm radius and 20 mm length, whose centre line runs perpendicular to the mounting face and whose mid-point coincides with the centre of the sphere.
condition: if three uniaxial accelerometers are used

text: In the child headform impactor, the remaining uniaxial accelerometers shall have their sensitive axes perpendicular to each other and parallel to the mounting face A, with their seismic mass positioned within a spherical tolerance field of 10 mm radius centred on the centre of the sphere.
condition: if three uniaxial accelerometers are used

text: The instrumentation response value CFC, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, of the child headform impactor shall be 1,000.
The CAC response value, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, of the child headform impactor shall be 500g for the acceleration.
The first natural frequency of the child headform impactor shall be over 5,000 Hz.
The adult headform impactor shall be made of aluminium, be of homogenous construction and be of spherical shape.
The overall diameter of the adult headform impactor is 165 ± 1 mm as shown in Figure 19.
The mass of the adult headform impactor shall be 4.5 ± 0.1 kg.
The moment of inertia of the adult headform impactor about an axis through the centre of gravity and perpendicular to the direction of impact shall be within the range of 0.010 to 0.013 kgm2.
The centre of gravity of the adult headform impactor including instrumentation shall be located in the geometric centre of the sphere with a tolerance of ± 5 mm.
The adult headform impactor sphere shall be covered with a 14 ± 0.5 mm thick synthetic skin, which shall cover at least half of the sphere.

A recess in the adult headform impactor sphere shall allow for mounting one triaxial or three uniaxial accelerometers within ± 10 mm seismic mass location tolerance from the centre of the sphere for the measurement axis, and ± 1 mm for the perpendicular direction to the measurement axis.

In the adult headform impactor, one of the uniaxial accelerometers shall have its sensitive axis perpendicular to the mounting face A and its seismic mass positioned within a cylindrical tolerance field of 1 mm radius and 20 mm length, whose centre line runs perpendicular to the mounting face and whose mid-point coincides with the centre of the sphere.
condition: if three uniaxial accelerometers are used

text: In the adult headform impactor, the remaining uniaxial accelerometers shall have their sensitive axes perpendicular to each other and parallel to the mounting face A, with their seismic mass positioned within a spherical tolerance field of 10 mm radius centred on the centre of the sphere.
condition: if three uniaxial accelerometers are used

text: The instrumentation response value CFC, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, of the adult headform impactor shall be 1,000.
The CAC response value, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, of the adult headform impactor shall be 500g for the acceleration.
The first natural frequency of the adult headform impactor shall be over 5,000 Hz.

A rear flat face shall be provided on the outer surface of the headform impactors which is perpendicular to the direction of travel, typically perpendicular to the axis of one of the accelerometers, and is a flat plate capable of providing access to the accelerometers and an attachment point for the propulsion system.
The headform impactors shall meet the performance requirements specified in paragraph 8.
The certified headform impactors may be used for a maximum of 20 impacts before re-certification.
The headform impactors shall be re-certified if more than one year has elapsed since the previous certification.
condition: if more than one year has elapsed since the previous certification

text: The headform impactors shall be re-certified if the transducer output, in any impact, has exceeded the specified CAC.
condition: if the transducer output has exceeded the specified CAC

text: Each flexible lower legform impactor to bumper test shall be completed within two hours of when the impactor to be used is removed from the controlled storage area.
The selected target points for the flexible lower legform impactor to bumper test shall be in the bumper test area.

The direction of the impact velocity vector of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be in the horizontal plane and parallel to the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ± 2° in the horizontal and longitudinal plane at the time of first contact.
The axis of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be perpendicular to the horizontal plane, with a roll and pitch angle tolerance of ± 2° in the lateral and longitudinal plane.

The bottom of the flexible lower legform impactor (without parts needed for launching and/or protection) shall be 75 mm above the ground reference plane at the time of first contact with the bumper, with a tolerance of ± 10 mm.
When setting the height of the propulsion system for the flexible lower legform impactor, an allowance shall be made for the influence of gravity during the period of free flight of the impactor.
The lower legform impactor for the bumper tests shall be in free flight at the moment of impact.

The lower legform impactor shall be released to free flight at such a distance from the vehicle that the test results are not influenced by contact of the impactor with the propulsion system during the rebound of the impactor.
The lower legform impactor may be propelled by any means only if it can be shown to meet the requirements of the test.

At the time of first contact the flexible lower legform impactor shall have the intended orientation about its vertical axis, for the correct operation of its knee joint, with a yaw angle tolerance of ± 5°.
At the time of first contact the centre line of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be within a ± 10 mm tolerance to the selected impact location.
During contact between the flexible lower legform impactor and the vehicle, the impactor shall not contact the ground or any object which is not part of the vehicle.
The impact velocity of the flexible lower legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s.
The effect of gravity shall be taken into account when the flexible lower legform impactor impact velocity is obtained from measurements taken before the time of first contact.
condition: if the impact velocity is obtained from measurements taken before first contact

text: The flexible lower legform impactor tibia bending moments shall not exceed ± 15 Nm within an evaluation interval of 30 ms immediately prior to impact.
The offset compensation shall be done with the flexible lower legform impactor in resting position prior to the test / acceleration phase.
Each upper legform to bumper test shall be completed within two hours of when the impactor to be used is removed from the controlled storage area.
The selected target points for the upper legform to bumper test shall be in the bumper test area.

The direction of impact of the upper legform impactor shall be parallel to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, with the axis of the upper legform vertical at the time of first contact, with a tolerance of ± 2°.
At the time of first contact the upper legform impactor centre line shall be vertically midway between the upper bumper reference line and the lower bumper reference line with a + 10 mm tolerance.
At the time of first contact the upper legform impactor vertical centre line shall be positioned laterally with the selected impact location with a tolerance of ± 10 mm.
The impact velocity of the upper legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s.

The headform impactors shall be in free flight at the moment of impact, at the required impact velocity (as specified in paragraphs 7.3.4. and 7.4.4.) and the required direction of impact (as specified in paragraphs 7.3.5. and 7.4.5.).

The headform impactors shall be released to free flight at such a distance from the vehicle that the test results are not influenced by contact of the impactor with the propulsion system during rebound of the impactor.
The velocity of the headform impactor shall be measured at some point during the free flight before impact, in accordance with the method specified in ISO 3784:1976.
The accuracy of the headform impactor velocity measurement shall be ± 0.01 m/sec.

The measured headform velocity shall be adjusted considering all factors which may affect the impactor between the point of measurement and the point of impact, in order to determine the velocity of the impactor at the time of impact.
The angle of the headform impactor velocity vector at the time of impact shall be calculated or measured.
In headform tests the acceleration time histories shall be recorded, and HIC shall be calculated.
In headform tests the first point of contact on the front structure of the vehicle shall be recorded.
Recording of headform test results shall be in accordance with ISO 6487:2002.
Child headform tests shall be made to the front structure within the boundaries of the child headform test area.
For child headform tests on the rear area of the bonnet top, the headform impactor shall not contact the windscreen or A-pillar before impacting the bonnet top.
condition: for tests on the rear area of the bonnet top

text: No child headform impact point shall be located so that the impactor will impact the test area with a glancing blow resulting in a more severe second impact outside the test area.

Selected impact points on the bonnet for the child headform impactor shall be, at the time of first contact, a minimum of 82.5 mm inside the defined side reference lines, set with a flexible tape held tautly along the outer surface of the vehicle.

Selected impact points on the bonnet for the child headform impactor shall be, at the time of first contact, forward of the WAD1700 line, or a minimum of 82.5 mm forwards of the bonnet rear reference line, whichever is most forward at the point of measurement, set with a flexible tape held tautly along the outer surface of the vehicle.

Selected impact points on the bonnet for the child headform impactor shall be, at the time of first contact, rearward of the WAD1000 line, or a minimum of 82.5 mm rearwards of the bonnet leading edge reference line, whichever is most rearward at the point of measurement, set with a flexible tape held tautly along the outer surface of the vehicle.
The point of first contact of the child headform impactor shall be within a ± 10 mm tolerance to the selected impact point.
The child headform velocity at the time of impact shall be 9.7 ± 0.2 m/s.
The direction of impact of the child headform shall be in the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle to be tested at an angle of 50 ± 2° to the horizontal.
The direction of impact of child headform tests to the front structure shall be downward and rearward.
Adult headform tests shall be made to the front structure within the boundaries of the adult headform test area.
For adult headform tests at the rear of the bonnet top, the headform impactor shall not contact the windscreen or A-pillar before impacting the bonnet top.
condition: for tests at the rear of the bonnet top

text: No adult headform impact point shall be located so that the impactor will impact the test area with a glancing blow resulting in a more severe second impact outside the test area.

Selected impact points on the bonnet for the adult headform impactor shall be, at the time of first contact, a minimum of 82.5 mm inside the defined side reference lines, set with a flexible tape held tautly along the outer surface of the vehicle.

Selected impact points on the bonnet for the adult headform impactor shall be, at the time of first contact, forward of the WAD2100 line, or a minimum of 82.5 mm forward of the bonnet rear reference line, whichever is most forward at the point of measurement, set with a flexible tape held tautly along the outer surface of the vehicle.
Selected impact points on the bonnet for the adult headform impactor shall be, at the time of first contact, rearward of the WAD1700 line.
The point of first contact of the adult headform impactor shall be within a ± 10 mm tolerance to the selected impact point.
The adult headform velocity at the time of impact shall be 9.7 ± 0.2 m/s.
The direction of impact of the adult headform shall be in the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle to be tested at an angle of 65° ± 2° to the horizontal.
The direction of impact of adult headform tests to the front structure shall be downward and rearward.

The impactors used in the tests described in this gtr are required to comply with the certification performance requirements of paragraphs 8.1 (lower legform), 8.2 (upper legform) and 8.3 (adult and child headform).
The femur and the tibia of the flexible lower legform impactor shall meet the requirements of paragraph 8.1.1.2. when tested according to paragraph 8.1.1.4.
The knee joint of the flexible lower legform impactor shall meet the requirements of paragraph 8.1.1.3. when tested according to paragraph 8.1.1.5.
The stabilized temperature of the flexible lower legform impactor during the static certification tests shall be 20° ± 2°C.
In the flexible lower legform static certification tests the CAC response values, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 30 mm for the knee ligament elongations and 4 kN for the applied external load.

For the flexible lower legform static certification tests, low-pass filtering at an appropriate frequency is permitted only to remove higher frequency noise without significantly affecting the measurement of the response of the impactor.
condition: if low-pass filtering is used

text: When the femur and the tibia of the flexible lower legform impactor, without flesh and skin, are loaded in bending in accordance with paragraph 8.1.1.4., the applied moment and the generated deflection at the centre of the femur and the tibia (Mc and Dc) shall be within the corridors shown in Figure 22.

When the knee joint of the flexible lower legform impactor, without flesh and skin, is loaded in bending in accordance with paragraph 8.1.1.5., the MCL, ACL and PCL elongations and applied bending moment or the force at the centre of the knee joint (Mc or Fc) shall be within the corridors shown in Figure 23.

In the femur and tibia static certification test, the edges of the femur and tibia, without flesh and skin, not bending parts shall be mounted to the support rig firmly as shown in Figure 24 and Figure 25.
In the femur and tibia static certification test, the Y-axis of the impactor shall be parallel to the loading axis within 180 ± 2° tolerance.
In the femur and tibia static certification test, low friction PTFE plastic pads are used under each support to obtain repeatable loading.
In the femur and tibia static certification test, the centre of the loading force shall be applied at the centre of the femur and the tibia within ± 2 mm tolerance along the Z-axis.

In the femur and tibia static certification test, the force shall be increased so as to maintain a deflection rate between 10 and 100 mm/minute until the bending moment at the centre part (Mc) of the femur or tibia reaches 380 Nm.
In the knee joint static certification test, the ends of the knee joint, without flesh and skin, shall be mounted to the support rig firmly as shown in Figure 26.
In the knee joint static certification test, the Y-axis of the impactor shall be parallel to the loading axis within ± 2° tolerance.
In the knee joint static certification test, low friction PTFE plastic pads are used under each support to obtain repeatable loading.

In the knee joint static certification test, to avoid impactor damage, a foamed neoprene sheet shall be set between the loading ram and the knee joint, and the impactor face of the knee joint described in Figure 26 shall be removed.
The foamed neoprene sheet used in the knee joint static certification test shall have compression characteristics as shown in Figure 15.
In the knee joint static certification test, the centre of the loading force shall be applied at the knee joint centre within ± 2 mm tolerance along the Z-axis.

In the knee joint static certification test, the external load shall be increased so as to maintain a deflection rate between 10 and 100 mm/minute until the bending moment at the centre part of the knee joint (Mc) reaches 400 Nm.
The assembled flexible lower legform impactor shall meet the requirements of paragraph 8.1.2.3. when tested as specified in paragraph 8.1.2.4. (pendulum test).
The test facility used for the flexible lower legform pendulum certification test shall have a stabilized temperature of 20 ± 2 °C during the test.
The temperature of the certification area shall be measured at the time of the flexible lower legform pendulum certification and recorded in a certification report.
In the pendulum certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform tibia at Tibia-1 shall be 235 Nm ≤ 272 Nm.
In the pendulum certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform tibia at Tibia-2 shall be 187 Nm ≤ 219 Nm.
In the pendulum certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform tibia at Tibia-3 shall be 139 Nm ≤ 166 Nm.
In the pendulum certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform tibia at Tibia-4 shall be 90 Nm ≤ 111 Nm.
In the pendulum certification test, the absolute value of the maximum MCL elongation of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be 20.5 ≤ 24.0 mm.
In the pendulum certification test, the absolute value of the maximum ACL elongation of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be 8.0 ≤ 10.5 mm.
In the pendulum certification test, the absolute value of the maximum PCL elongation of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be 3.5 ≤ 5.0 mm.
For the pendulum certification maximum bending moment and maximum elongation values, the readings used shall be from the initial impact timing to 200 ms after the impact timing.
In the flexible lower legform pendulum certification test, the instrumentation response value CFC, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 180 for all transducers.

In the flexible lower legform pendulum certification test, the CAC response values, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 30 mm for the knee ligament elongations and 400 Nm for the tibia bending moments.

In the pendulum certification test, the flexible lower legform impactor, including the flesh and skin, shall be suspended from the dynamic certification test rig 15 ± 1° upward from the horizontal as shown in Figure 27.
In the pendulum certification test, the flexible lower legform impactor shall be released from the suspended position and fall freely against the pin joint of the test rig as shown in Figure 27.
In the pendulum certification test, the knee joint centre of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be 30 ± 1 mm below the bottom line of the stopper bar when the impactor is hanging freely.
In the pendulum certification test, the tibia impact face without the flesh and skin shall be located 13 ± 2 mm from the front upper edge of the stopper bar when the impactor is hanging freely.
The assembled flexible lower legform impactor shall meet the requirements of paragraph 8.1.3.3. when tested as specified in paragraph 8.1.3.4. (inverse test).
The test facility used for the flexible lower legform inverse certification test shall have a stabilized temperature of 20 ± 2 °C during the test.
The temperature of the certification area shall be measured at the time of the flexible lower legform inverse certification and recorded in a certification report.
In the inverse certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform tibia at Tibia-1 shall be 230 Nm ≤ 272 Nm.
In the inverse certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform tibia at Tibia-2 shall be 210 Nm ≤ 252 Nm.
In the inverse certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform tibia at Tibia-3 shall be 166 Nm ≤ 192 Nm.
In the inverse certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform tibia at Tibia-4 shall be 93 Nm ≤ 108 Nm.
In the inverse certification test, the absolute value of the maximum MCL elongation of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be 17.0 ≤ 21.0 mm.
In the inverse certification test, the absolute value of the maximum ACL elongation of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be 8.0 ≤ 10 mm.
In the inverse certification test, the absolute value of the maximum PCL elongation of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be 4.0 ≤ 6.0 mm.
For the inverse certification maximum bending moment and maximum elongation values, the readings used shall be from the initial impact timing to 50 ms after the impact timing.
In the flexible lower legform inverse certification test, the instrumentation response value CFC, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 180 for all transducers.

In the flexible lower legform inverse certification test, the CAC response values, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 30 mm for the knee ligament elongations and 400 Nm for the tibia bending moments.
In the inverse certification test, the assembled flexible lower legform impactor (with the flesh and skin) shall be hung vertically and freely suspended from a test rig as shown in Figure 28.

In the inverse certification test, the flexible lower legform impactor is impacted by the upper edge of a linearly guided aluminium honeycomb impactor, covered by a thin paper cloth with a maximum thickness of 1 mm, at an impact speed of 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s.
In the inverse certification test, the legform shall achieve a free flight condition within 10 ms after the time of first contact of the honeycomb impactor.
The 5052 alloy honeycomb attached in front of the moving ram in the inverse certification test shall be 200 ± 5 mm wide, 160 ± 5 mm high and 60 ± 2 mm deep.
The honeycomb used in the inverse certification test shall have a crush strength of 517.1 kPa ± 10 per cent (75 psi ± 10 per cent).

The honeycomb used in the inverse certification test should have cell sizes of either 4.76 mm (3/16 inch) with a density of 32.0 kg/m³ (2.0 pcf) or 6.35 mm (1/4 inch) with a density of 36.8 kg/m³ (2.3 pcf).
In the inverse certification test, the upper edge of the honeycomb face shall be in line with the rigid plate of the linearly guided impactor.
At the time of first contact in the inverse certification test, the upper edge of the honeycomb shall be in line with the knee joint centre line within a vertical tolerance of ± 2 mm.
The honeycomb shall not be deformed before the inverse certification impact test.

At the time of first contact in the inverse certification test, the flexible lower legform impactor pitch angle (rotation around the Y-axis), and therefore the pitch angle of the velocity vector of the honeycomb impactor, shall be within a tolerance of ± 2° in relation to the lateral vertical plane.

At the time of first contact in the inverse certification test, the flexible lower legform impactor roll angle (rotation around the X-axis), and therefore the roll angle of the honeycomb impactor, shall be within a tolerance of ± 2° in relation to the longitudinal vertical plane.

At the time of first contact in the inverse certification test, the flexible lower legform impactor yaw angle (rotation around the Z-axis), and therefore the yaw angle of the velocity vector of the honeycomb impactor, shall be within a tolerance of ± 2°.
The upper legform impactor shall meet the requirements of paragraph 8.2.3. when tested as specified in paragraph 8.2.4.

The foam flesh for the upper legform impactor shall be stored for a period of at least four hours in a controlled storage area with a stabilized humidity of 35 ± 10 percent and a stabilized temperature of 20° ± 2°C prior to impactor removal for calibration.
The upper legform test impactor itself shall have a temperature of 20° ± 2°C at the time of impact during calibration.
The temperature tolerances for the upper legform test impactor shall apply at a relative humidity of 40 ± 30 percent after a soak period of at least four hours prior to their application in a test.
The test facility used for the upper legform calibration test shall have a stabilized humidity of 40 ± 30 percent and a stabilized temperature of 20° ± 4°C during calibration.
Each upper legform calibration shall be completed within two hours of when the impactor to be calibrated is removed from the controlled storage area.
The relative humidity and temperature of the upper legform calibration area shall be measured at the time of calibration and recorded in the calibration report.
When the upper legform impactor is propelled into a stationary cylindrical pendulum, the peak force measured in each load transducer shall be not less than 1.20 kN and not more than 1.55 kN.
In the upper legform certification test, the difference between the peak forces measured in the top and bottom load transducers shall not be more than 0.10 kN.
In the upper legform certification test, the peak bending moment measured by the strain gauges shall not be less than 190 Nm and not more than 250 Nm on the centre position.
In the upper legform certification test, the peak bending moment measured by the strain gauges shall not be less than 160 Nm and not more than 220 Nm for the outer positions.
In the upper legform certification test, the difference between the upper and lower peak bending moments shall not be more than 20 Nm.
For the upper legform certification values, the readings used shall be from the initial impact with the pendulum and not from the arresting phase.
Any system used to arrest the upper legform impactor or pendulum shall be so arranged that the arresting phase does not overlap in time with the initial impact.
condition: if an arresting system is used

text: The arresting system shall not cause the upper legform transducer outputs to exceed the specified CAC.
condition: if an arresting system is used

text: In the upper legform certification test, the instrumentation response value CFC, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 180 for all transducers.
In the upper legform certification test, the CAC response values, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 10 kN for the force transducers and 1000 Nm for the bending moment measurements.
In the upper legform certification test, the impactor shall be mounted to the propulsion and guidance system by a torque limiting joint.

In the upper legform certification test, the torque limiting joint shall be set so that the longitudinal axis of the front member is perpendicular to the axis of the guidance system, with a tolerance of ± 2°.
In the upper legform certification test, the torque limiting joint friction torque shall be set to a minimum of 650 Nm but no more than 850 Nm.

In the upper legform certification test, the guidance system shall be fitted with low friction guides that allow the impactor to move only in the specified direction of impact, when in contact with the pendulum.

For the upper legform certification test, the impactor mass shall be adjusted to give a mass of 12 ± 0.1 kg, including those propulsion and guidance components which are effectively part of the impactor during impact.

For the upper legform certification test, the centre of gravity of those parts of the impactor which are effectively forward of the torque limiting joint, including the extra masses fitted, shall lie on the longitudinal centreline of the impactor, with a tolerance of ± 10 mm.
The upper legform impactor shall be certified with previously unused foam.
The upper legform impactor foam shall not be excessively handled or deformed before, during or after fitting.
In the upper legform certification test, the impactor with the front member vertical shall be propelled horizontally at a velocity of 7.1 ± 0.1 m/s into the stationary pendulum.
The pendulum tube for the upper legform certification test shall have a mass of 3 ± 0.03 kg, a wall thickness of 3 ± 0.15 mm and an outside diameter of 150 mm +1 mm/-4 mm.
The total pendulum tube length for the upper legform certification test shall be 275 ± 25 mm.
The pendulum tube shall be made from cold finished seamless steel (metal surface plating is permissible for protection from corrosion), with an outer surface finish of better than 2.0 micrometer.
The pendulum tube shall be suspended on two wire ropes of 1.5 ± 0.2 mm diameter and of 2.0 m minimum length.
The surface of the pendulum shall be clean and dry.

The pendulum tube shall be positioned so that the longitudinal axis of the cylinder is perpendicular to the front member (i.e. level), with a tolerance of ± 2°, and to the direction of impactor motion, with a tolerance of ± 2°.
The centre of the pendulum tube shall be aligned with the centre of the upper legform impactor front member, with tolerances of ± 5 mm laterally and ± 5 mm vertically.
The child and adult headform impactors shall meet the requirements specified in paragraph 8.3.2. when tested as specified in paragraph 8.3.3.
In the certification drop test, the headform impactors shall be dropped from a height of 376 ± 1 mm in accordance with paragraph 8.3.3.

When dropped from a height of 376 ± 1 mm, the peak resultant acceleration measured by one triaxial (or three uniaxial) accelerometer(s) in the child headform impactor shall be not less than 245g and not more than 300g.

When dropped from a height of 376 ± 1 mm, the peak resultant acceleration measured by one triaxial (or three uniaxial) accelerometer(s) in the adult headform impactor shall be not less than 225g and not more than 275g.
In the headform impactor drop test, the acceleration time curve shall be uni-modal.
In the headform impactor certification test, the instrumentation response value CFC for each accelerometer shall be 1,000 Hz as defined in ISO 6487:2002.
In the headform impactor certification test, the instrumentation response value CAC for each accelerometer shall be 500g as defined in ISO 6487:2002.
The headform impactors shall have a temperature of 20 ± 2°C at the time of impact in the certification test.
The headform impactor temperature tolerances shall apply at a relative humidity of 40 ± 30 percent after a soak period of at least four hours prior to their application in a test.
After complying with the certification test, each headform impactor can be used for a maximum of 20 impact tests.
For the certification drop test, the headform impactor shall be suspended from a drop rig as shown in Figure 30.
The headform impactor shall be dropped from the specified height by means that ensure instant release.

The headform impactor shall be dropped onto a rigidly supported flat horizontal steel plate, over 50 mm thick and over 300 x 300 mm square, which has a clean dry surface and a surface finish of between 0.2 and 2.0 micrometers.
The child headform impactor shall be dropped with the rear face of the impactor at the test angle specified in paragraph 7.3.5. with respect to the vertical as shown in Figure 30.
The adult headform impactor shall be dropped with the rear face of the impactor at the test angle specified in paragraph 7.4.5. with respect to the vertical as shown in Figure 30.
The suspension of the headform impactor shall be such that it does not rotate during the fall.
The headform impactor drop test shall be performed three times, with the headform impactor rotated 120° around its symmetrical axis after each test.
If all of the prerequisites of Annex 1 are met, the vehicle shall be tested with the DPPS activated as intended for the entire headform test area.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS and all prerequisites are met

text: Based on a determination by each Contracting Party, a Contracting Party may either allow static tests, dynamic tests and a combination thereof, or stipulate dynamic tests only for the DPPS.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The vehicle manufacturer shall identify the detailed information highlighted in Annex 1, including all necessary information regarding detection of pedestrians and the deployment of the system, before any testing of the DPPS begins.
condition: if the DPPS is to be assessed statically, dynamically or combined

text: In case of HIT_d < TRT, the headform test on the DPPS shall be performed dynamically.
condition: HIT_d < TRT

text: In case of HIT_d ≥ TRT, the headform test on the DPPS may be performed either statically at a height no more than the deployed position or dynamically.
condition: HIT_d ≥ TRT

text: If any of the prerequisites from paragraphs 1.2 to 1.7 of Annex 1 are not met, the vehicle shall be tested with the DPPS in the undeployed position.
condition: if any DPPS prerequisite is not met

text: As a Contracting Party option, a technical description of the DPPS components shall be identified by the manufacturer, accompanied by the information listed in paragraphs 1.2.1 and 1.2.2.
condition: as a Contracting Party option

text: The DPPS technical description shall include, for the sensing system, the sensor type (e.g. pressure, optical, acceleration, etc.).
condition: as a Contracting Party option

text: The DPPS technical description shall include, for the sensing system, the sensor locations.
condition: as a Contracting Party option

text: The DPPS technical description shall include, for the sensing system, the operation process including the lower deployment threshold speed of the DPPS.
condition: as a Contracting Party option

text: The DPPS deployment information shall include the technology of the DPPS (airbag, active bonnet, etc.).
condition: as a Contracting Party option

text: The DPPS deployment information shall include a mechanism explanation.
condition: as a Contracting Party option

text: The DPPS deployment information shall include a component description (lifting system (e.g. actuator), hinge, latch, etc.).
condition: as a Contracting Party option

text: The DPPS deployment information shall include deployed position information (not required for dynamic testing).
condition: as a Contracting Party option; not for dynamic testing

text: The DPPS deployment information shall include TRT information with ST and DT separately (for dynamic testing, ST only).
condition: as a Contracting Party option

text: The DPPS deployment information shall include the evolution of system stability (e.g. pressure or force versus time diagram), for static testing only.
condition: as a Contracting Party option; static testing only

text: The marking of the headform test areas of the DPPS shall always be done in undeployed position, for static, dynamic or combined testing.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: For the headform test for protection below the lower deployment threshold speed of the DPPS, the vehicle outer surface shall remain in undeployed position.
condition: headform test below the lower deployment threshold speed

text: For the headform test below the lower deployment threshold speed, the test procedures of paragraphs 7.2. to 7.4. shall apply with the impact speed specified at 0.9 times the lower deployment threshold speed.
condition: headform test below the lower deployment threshold speed

text: For the headform test below the lower deployment threshold speed, the allocation of the HIC1700 and HIC1000 Zones may differ from those at nominal velocity (9.7 m/s) headform impact tests according to paragraph 5.2.4.
condition: headform test below the lower deployment threshold speed

text: In the headform test below the lower deployment threshold speed of the DPPS, the HIC shall comply with paragraph 5.2.3.
condition: headform test below the lower deployment threshold speed

text: The HBM shall be qualified according to Addendum 5 of Mutual Resolution No. 1 (M.R.1).
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: HIT information shall be documented according to Annex 2.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: For deployed static tests, the Deployed Position, Maximum Deployment Height, ST and DT specified by the manufacturer shall be verified using appropriate tracking means, such as high-speed videos, accelerometer, or laser at the reference points indicated by the manufacturer (on the lifting devices).
condition: deployed static tests

text: The tolerance for the verified ST is -5 ms/+3 ms on the specified value, and the tolerances for Deployed Position, Maximum Deployment Height and DT are ±20 percent on the specified values.
condition: deployed static tests

text: If a measured value is within the defined tolerances, the value specified by the manufacturer shall be used; otherwise the measured value shall be used.
condition: deployed static tests

text: The vehicle manufacturer shall specify the lowest speed of activation (lower deployment velocity threshold) of the DPPS.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: For the system deployment verification, sensor activation tests with the FlexPLI, as specified in paragraph 6.3.1.1., shall be performed within the detection test area at the DPPS lower deployment velocity threshold.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: A sensing system verification test with the FlexPLI shall be performed at nominal velocity (11.1 m/s) at vehicle centreline (Y0).
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: Where a sensing verification test is performed within the tolerances of paragraph 3 of Annex 1 but below the lower deployment velocity threshold or outside the detection test area and the system does not deploy, the test must be repeated.
condition: test below the threshold or outside the detection test area and no deployment

text: If the DPPS is not activated during any of the verification tests, all headform tests shall be conducted in undeployed position according to paragraphs 7.2. to 7.4.
condition: if the system is not activated during any verification test

text: For sensing verification tests with stationary vehicle, the vehicle shall be set to the normal running condition as specified by the manufacturer for a vehicle speed corresponding to the particular use case.
condition: tests with stationary vehicle

text: The TRT shall be confirmed by using the FlexPLI at the vehicle speed of 11.1 m/s and at the vehicle centreline (Y0).
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The ST is measured either independently or during a TRT measurement test, at the vehicle speed specified in this Regulation and at the vehicle centreline (Y0).
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: If the measured ST is within a tolerance of -5 ms/+3 ms, the value specified by the manufacturer shall be used; otherwise the measured value shall be used for the test.
For dynamic testing, only ST shall be verified.
condition: dynamic testing

text: For TRT/ST verification tests with stationary vehicle, the vehicle shall be set to the normal running condition as specified by the manufacturer.
condition: tests with stationary vehicle

text: For FlexPLI verification tests with a moving vehicle impacting the stationary impactor, the target speed tolerance shall be ±0.6 m/s.
condition: moving vehicle impacting stationary impactor

text: For FlexPLI verification tests with a moving vehicle impacting the stationary impactor, the impact accuracy tolerance shall be ±50 mm.
condition: moving vehicle impacting stationary impactor

text: For FlexPLI verification tests with a propulsion system propelling the impactor against the stationary vehicle, the target speed, impact accuracy and angle tolerances shall be those of the performance tests in paragraph 7.1.
condition: impactor propelled against stationary vehicle

text: For headform tests on the DPPS at nominal velocity (9.7 m/s), the selection of impact points and the allocation of the HIC1700 and HIC1000 zones shall always be based on and related to the test area with undeployed DPPS.
condition: headform tests at nominal velocity on DPPS

text: If the vehicle manufacturer opts for the static test procedure, the conditions of paragraphs 4.1.1 to 4.1.4 shall be fulfilled; if so, the headform tests on the headform test area shall be performed statically.
condition: if the manufacturer opts for the static test procedure

text: If any of the static test conditions are not met, the headform tests on the headform test area shall be performed dynamically.
condition: if any static test condition is not met

text: All headform tests may be performed statically only where the vehicle manufacturer has demonstrated by numerical simulations on the deployed DPPS that HIT_d ≥ TRT for the smallest selected pedestrian stature, as defined in Annex 2.
condition: static test option

text: For static tests, the vehicle outer surface shall represent the deployed position within the specified tolerances, while the resisting force is considered.
condition: static test option

text: When there is a constraint on time for the stability of the system and HIT_d ≥ TRT, the launching time of the headform impactor shall ensure that the system remains stable (tolerance ±10 per cent of corresponding resisting force), as identified by the manufacturer.
condition: static time constraint and HIT_d ≥ TRT

text: During the static tests it shall be ensured that the resisting force of the DPPS is equivalent to the actual situation at HIT.
condition: static tests

text: Appropriate means (e.g. actuator surrogates) may be used to ensure that the corresponding resisting force of the DPPS is reached.
condition: static tests

text: For static tests on the DPPS, the test procedures specified in paragraphs 7.2. to 7.4. shall apply.
condition: static tests

text: Prior to conducting the static tests at 9.7 m/s, one headform test at the discretion of the test laboratory may be conducted on the undeployed DPPS to confirm that impact velocity and impact location are within tolerances.
condition: static tests

text: If the tolerances for impact speed and location are met during the test on the undeployed DPPS, there is no requirement to prove that these tolerances are still met during the static tests, provided that test inputs remain the same.
condition: static tests, test inputs unchanged

text: Alternative methods to demonstrate the test accuracy of static tests may also be accepted.
condition: static tests

text: In the dynamic test, the headform launch device and DPPS deployment shall be synchronised to achieve the correct HIT_s.
condition: dynamic test option

text: Prior to conducting the dynamic tests at 9.7 m/s, one headform test at the discretion of the test laboratory shall be conducted on the undeployed DPPS to confirm that impact velocity and impact location are within tolerances.
condition: dynamic tests

text: If the tolerances for impact speed and location are met during the undeployed test, there is no requirement to meet these tolerances during dynamic tests, provided test inputs remain the same.
condition: dynamic tests, test inputs unchanged

text: For dynamic testing, HIT_s shall be established from the HIT_s versus WAD graph obtained from Annex 2, Figure 2-3.
condition: dynamic tests

text: For dynamic testing, ST shall be determined from the manufacturer prerequisite or the sensor verification test carried out at the vehicle centreline (Y0).
condition: dynamic tests

text: The test facility shall ensure that the head impact occurs at the correct time relative to the deployment of the DPPS, taking into account the HIT_s for the corresponding WAD of the head impact point and ST, with Fire Delay = Launching Duration Headform Impactor – (HIT_s – ST).
condition: dynamic tests

text: Combined static and dynamic tests may apply at the manufacturer's choice; where the headform test area has sections with HIT_d < TRT and sections with HIT_d ≥ TRT, all test points forward of the corresponding WAD (HIT_d < TRT) shall be tested dynamically.
condition: combined test option

text: In combined testing, the remaining section of the headform test area (HIT_d ≥ TRT) may be tested statically.
condition: combined test option

text: Pedestrian HBMs required for GTR No. 9 shall be selected from the following statures: six-year-old (6YO), 5th percentile female (AF05), 50th percentile male (AM50) and 95th percentile male (AM95).
It shall be ensured that the HBMs used in Annex 2 comply with all requirements within Addendum 5 of Mutual Resolution No. 1 (M.R.1).
The HBM qualification results shall be documented as specified in Addendum 5 of M.R.1.
Only those HBM statures selected according to paragraph 2.2. of Annex 2 shall be qualified.
The qualified pedestrian HBM shall be the very same model as used for HIT determination simulations, with the same version of the HBM.
The qualified pedestrian HBM and the HBM used for HIT determination simulations shall have the same node-position of every single node.
The qualified pedestrian HBM and the HBM used for HIT determination simulations shall have identical material cards (including fracture mode), contact cards, control cards and constraints.
The qualified pedestrian HBM and the HBM used for HIT determination simulations shall have identical initial element stresses/strains.
condition: if available

text: The qualified pedestrian HBM and the HBM used for HIT determination simulations shall have identical initial contact penetrations/contact forces.
condition: if available

text: All simulations (qualification and HIT determination) shall be performed with consistent solver-version and type (e.g. processing type, precision, parallelisation).
All simulations (qualification and HIT determination) shall be performed with a consistent time-step.
All simulations (qualification and HIT determination) shall be performed with consistent time-step settings (relating to initial and dynamic mass scaling).
All simulations (qualification and HIT determination) shall be performed with consistent contact settings between HBM and vehicle.
All simulations (qualification and HIT determination) shall be performed with consistent control settings affecting the pedestrian model.

Pedestrian models for HIT determination simulations shall be selected from the following statures: a six-year-old (6YO), 5th percentile female (AF05), 50th percentile male (AM50) and 95th percentile male (AM95).
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The pedestrian position and stance used in the HBM shall be as defined in Addendum 5 of M.R.1.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The pedestrian model has to be positioned such that the head centre of gravity (CoG) is aligned with the vehicle centreline.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The vehicle model has to be positioned in the setup such that the vehicle ground level is aligned with the ground level used in the qualification simulations.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: As described in Addendum 5 of M.R.1, the HBM shall be exposed to a vertical acceleration field constituting the gravitational loading.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: A local vehicle coordinate system has to be initially aligned with the global coordinate system defined in Addendum 5 of M.R.1 and shall be connected to the vehicle model CoG.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The initial speed of the vehicle model has to be prescribed and is 40 km/h for all HIT determination simulations.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The y and z motion of the vehicle model has to be constrained and the motion in x-direction must not be constrained.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The selected HBMs used to draw the WAD/HIT-line shall be those HBMs where the head hits the DPPS properly, i.e. there is a contact between the head and DPPS and at time of this contact the x-coordinate of the CoG of the head is between the smallest and largest x-coordinate of the DPPS at y=0.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: Simulations with the next tallest HBM shall also be performed, but only to prove that this HBM does not hit the DPPS properly.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: If only one HBM hits the DPPS properly, the next tallest HBM shall also belong to the selected HBMs.
condition: if only one HBM hits the DPPS properly

text: It shall be confirmed that time history curves of the x and z coordinates of HC and AC in the global coordinate system have been generated from each HIT determination simulation.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: It shall be confirmed that a time history curve of the x displacement of the vehicle CoG in the global coordinate system has been generated from each simulation.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: It shall be confirmed that a time history curve of the resultant acceleration of HC has been generated from each simulation.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: It shall be confirmed that time history curves of contact forces (between vehicle and HBM without upper extremities, vehicle and HBM head and total contact force) have been generated from each simulation.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: It shall be confirmed that time history curves of total hourglass and internal energies of the total setup have been generated from each simulation.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: It shall be confirmed that a time history curve of mass increase has been generated from each simulation.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: All simulation output time history curves shall be plotted every 0.1 ms or less.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: Animations of the simulations shall be generated with an output interval of 1 ms.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: A quality check shall be performed that the contact force between HBM and vehicle is zero at simulation start.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: A quality check shall be performed that the total energy remains constant within a 15 per cent tolerance.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: A quality check shall be performed that hourglass energy is ≤ 10 per cent of the total energy.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: A quality check shall be performed that artificial mass increase is less than 3 per cent.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The Head Impact Time shall be calculated as the elapsed time between the time of first contact of the HBM (neglecting forearms and hands) with the vehicle outer surface, being the first time where the contact force is not zero anymore, and the time of first contact of its head with the vehicle outer surface.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: If the HIT calculation method is for any reason not applicable, an appropriate alternative method may be applied and shall be reported.
condition: if the specified HIT calculation method is not applicable

text: For the determination of the WAD corresponding to HIT, the point (Xhead, 0, Zhead) of the CoG of the head at time of first head contact with the DPPS, in the local vehicle coordinate system, shall be projected orthogonally onto the surface of the undeployed vehicle, taking the projection point with the highest x value if there are multiple, and the WAD for this point shall be computed rounded to the nearest full millimetre.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The HIT determination simulation report shall document the date of report, the name of car manufacturer, the type and release version of software (FE-software package name, revision and version), the name and version of the HBM and the specification of the car.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: Images showing the front view and side view of the pedestrian, at t0 and at the time of head impact, shall be added to the report.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: For all simulations, Table 2-1 shall be filled in, checking consistency between qualification and HIT determination simulations for identical HBM, solver version, timestep and all other control settings.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: For all simulations, Table 2-2 Quality Checks shall be filled in.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The coefficient of friction between vehicle and HBM in the HIT determination simulation shall be 0.3.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The head centre of gravity shall be positioned at vehicle centreline Y=0 mm.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The contact force between HBM and vehicle at simulation start shall be 0.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The change in total energy throughout the simulation shall be ≤15%.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The amount of hourglass energy relative to total energy shall be ≤10%.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: The artificial mass increase relative to total mass of the setup shall be ≤3%.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: For the HBMs selected according to paragraph 2.2 of Annex 2, the computed HIT_d values and corresponding WADs from simulations on the DPPS in deployed mode have to be filled into Table 2-3.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: For the selected HBMs, the computed HIT_s values and corresponding WADs from simulations on the DPPS in undeployed mode have to be filled into Table 2-4; simulations on the undeployed DPPS are not required if HIT_d ≥ TRT for all HBMs.
condition: unless HIT_d ≥ TRT for all HBMs

text: For each simulation, the following diagrams shall be documented: ACx and HCx as a function of time; ACz and HCz as a function of time; HCz as a function of HCx and ACz as a function of ACx; total contact force between HBM and vehicle as a function of time; total, kinetic, internal and hourglass energy as a function of time.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: Based on the results of Table 2-3, a graph of WAD versus HIT_d shall be plotted using a linear regression line for comparison with TRT, as shown in Figure 2-2.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a DPPS

text: Based on the results of Table 2-4, a graph of WAD versus HIT_s shall be plotted using a linear regression line as shown in Figure 2-3.
condition: if simulations on the undeployed DPPS are performed

text: The WAD versus HIT_s regression lines have to be extrapolated in both directions.
condition: if simulations on the undeployed DPPS are performed
